rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a 2BB blastocyst, with reasonable comments on loose ICM and sparse TE, but it overstates certainty from a single image and adds less-verifiable details such as mild fragmentation/debris and timing interpretation.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor diagnosis, BMI, smoking, alcohol, sperm parameters, endometrium, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Overall structured and logical, but there are notable issues: it treats the embryo as a Day-4 transfer while also using blastocyst-stage assumptions, makes speculative inferences about the rest of the cohort, and applies quantitative lifestyle penalties with more precision than the data support.

Much of the counseling is evidence-based (single embryo viability, smoking/alcohol cessation, no bed rest), but some recommendations are weakly supported or not routine guideline-based, such as adding estradiol for low BMI, suggesting ERA after one failure, and broad PGT-A endorsement at age 33.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer support, lifestyle modification, and future-cycle planning, though a few suggestions are more speculative than standard practice.
